about: What the Tier 2 taste judge compares against (factory/panel.py). Tens are work Krish locked or picked as the bar; the bad anchors are read live from factory/floor.json, with his exact words, so they are never copied here. Add every new lock and every new decline the day it happens.

tens.what: Krish's twelve locked organic posts (factory/locks/): genre parody, a dog's inner voice, the real product at the end

"My dog's 9 to 5": a shepherd in a hoodie with a hidden person's arms stages every lyric of Dolly Parton's 9 to 5 literally, one beat a second; 18.8M views when read. Its lyric captions are never copied (Krish, 10 Nov: no lyric subtitles)
Two upright kittens do the viral 80s dance to Bronski Beat's Smalltown Boy into a low ultra-wide lens: a close-up each, then a synced two-shot
tens.why: Krish, 10 Nov: "We should Generate a realistic version of this with dog's"

questions_tier1.ask: Every dog has correct anatomy in every frame shown: four legs, one tail, paws with toes, two eyes and ears in place, no merged or extra limbs, human hands with five fingers. Answer no and name the frame if any frame fails.
With every caption and on-screen word covered, can you state the joke's payoff in one sentence from the pictures alone? Answer yes with the sentence, or no.
Is the premise readable in frame 1 alone, with the sound off, in under a second?
No on-screen word covers a dog's eyes, face or the main action in any frame.
No AI-drawn mug, blanket, portrait or card appears; any product shown is a clean store render on a plain ground with no words.
The same dog keeps the same coat, markings, collar and clothes across frames, and props do not change or vanish.
No on-screen text repeats a song lyric in any frame. A single opening premise line is allowed.
List every element on screen that is not the dog, its hands or the gag (text, overlays, props that do nothing). Answer yes only if each one earns its place; name any that does not.

tier2_rubric: Score 1 to 10 against the tens above in the same format. 10: it would beat the matching ten. 9: as good as it. 7 to 8: competent but forgettable. 6 or below: a floor anchor would apply. Name the ten you compared against, the single strongest beat with its frame, and, if below 9, the floor quote Krish would most likely say. Only 9 and above reach Krish.
